title: Lambert Analytics - Token Velocity & Hosting Mode Qualification
next_steps: Alex to send Dedicated vs Hosted TCO spreadsheet and pricing sheet (by 2028-07-03)
Priya to run a 1-hour token/sec benchmark with customer's 2k-token prompt on a p3-equivalent (by 2028-07-05)
Sana to receive SOC2/ISO + KMS and network architecture docs (Alex to attach)
Schedule technical deep-dive (SE-led) with infra team to review VPC peering and egress (week of 2028-07-09)
action_items: Alex Moreno - email SOC2 + KMS docs and security brief - 2028-07-02
Priya Shah - run stream and batch token/sec benchmark with 50 concurrent streams - 2028-07-05
Jordan Park - share current traffic profile and peak 1-min request rates - 2028-07-04
Maya Liu - provide representative prompt set (10 prompts, varying length) - 2028-07-03
summary: Discovery call to qualify latency/throughput needs. Lambert needs p95 sub-250ms for short chat flows and 95th-percentile under 800ms for long streaming interactions; they're evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private. Security and data residency are gating for production. Agreed to run benchmarks and share docs.
transcript: [00:00] Alex (AE): Hey everyone thanks for joining, i think we have about an hour, i'm alex from Redwood Inference, with me is priya our systems eng, how's everyone doing?
[00:06] Evan (CTO): Morning alex, good thanks. We gave you a lot of pre-read but wanted to run through latency and hosting options today.
[00:12] Priya (SE): hi all, quick agenda: 1) current infra and traffic, 2) p95 and streaming targets, 3) hosting mode tradeoffs, 4) next steps and benchmark plan.
[00:22] Tom (PM): yup that sounds right. i'll try to keep notes on the product side. Maya and Jordan are the deep techs here.
[00:27] Maya (ML Eng): hey, quick point — most defs our prompts vary 50-2k tokens depending on customer, ok to call that out.
[00:33] Jordan (Infra): also note: we have on prem datacenter in eu-west-1 and cloud in us-east for non-eu traffic — low tolerance for egress costs.
[00:40] Alex (AE): good, that helps. can you share p95 goals? i saw a note in the form but want to confirm live.

[00:46] Evan (CTO): for our short chat interactions, p95 should be below 250ms, ideally below 200ms. for longer streaming or summarizations, p95 under 800ms. concurrency spikes up to 200 simultaneous users, peak token/sec bursts up to ~15k tokens/sec across cluster.

[01:02] Priya (SE): ok two separate SLO buckets: low-latency short flows and longer streaming. what's your tolerance for graceful degradation? do you expect fallback to cheaper models when overloaded?
[01:12] Tom (PM): yes fallback is acceptable, but must be transparent to user and not drop below a baseline quality. also for EU customers data must stay in eu regions.

[01:21] Sana (Security): security check — we require SOC2-type controls, SSO with SAML, audit logs for all inference requests, and option to hold keys in our KMS/hsm. private deployment will be considered if hosted can't meet those.
[01:33] Alex (AE): understood, we do SOC2, SAML SSO, and KMS integrations; for private we offer a VPC-enabled control plane and on-prem package — i'll send the docs.
[01:40] Maya (ML Eng): curious about streaming: will the platform stream partial tokens back as soon as they're ready? low tail latency is critical for perceived responsiveness.

[01:47] Priya (SE): yes we support streaming chunked responses and function call style responses; we also do continuous batching and KV caching for repeated prefixes. Streaming does add some overhead but improves TTF first token dramatically.
[01:58] Jordan (Infra): what's the typical p95 for first token on a hosted small model? ballpark numbers help our capacity planning.

[02:06] Priya (SE): ballpark: for a 7B-family model hosted on our shared tier you'll see first-token p95 ~120-250ms depending on region and request size. For larger models 30B+ first token p95 is 300-600ms typical. Dedicated gives you predictable p95 closer to lower bound because of reserved GPU pools and pinning.
[02:22] Evan (CTO): how do you handle KV cache for multi-turn chat? we can't re-encode full history every time, that's expensive.

[02:28] Priya (SE): we keep a KV cache per session which avoids re-computing early layers; that reduces tokens/sec cost significantly for long multi-turn flows. We do prefix caching heuristics and TTLs.
[02:38] Tom (PM): about concurrency — our spikes are short, like 1-3 minutes, with 200 concurrent. do you recommend Hosted with burst or Dedicated reservation?

[02:46] Alex (AE): short bursts are common. Hosted with burst capacity can be fine but you pay surge pricing; Dedicated with autoscale and burst pools gives predictable latency and economics if spikes are sustained. For spikes that are <5% of daily traffic hosted is often cheaper.
[02:58] Maya (ML Eng): can we run a benchmark that mirrors our workload? we have variable prompt lengths, some streaming, some blocking generation.

[03:04] Priya (SE): absolutely. we prefer to run two benchmarks: 1) micro-benchmark for p95 first-token and end-to-end generation with representative prompts, 2) scale benchmark for concurrency and token/sec across multiple clients. We'll instrument token/sec and tail latency metrics.
[03:15] Jordan (Infra): network wise we need to see VPC peering options and egress patterns. If hosted requires cross-region egress for eu-data that won't fly.
[03:22] Sana (Security): yes we need contractual data residency. Does Redwood offer isolated eu-only hosted endpoints?
[03:27] Alex (AE): we have region-scoped hosted endpoints in eu-west. For stricter controls we recommend Dedicated in eu region or Private deploy behind your VPC.
[03:34] Evan (CTO): what about cold starts and model loading for large models? we can't afford a several-second cold start on a spike.

[03:40] Priya (SE): we keep warm GPUs and use smart routing; Dedicated allows pre-warmed model instances and faster cold start SLA. We also use lightweight quantized variants for faster loading if quality tradeoff is ok.
[03:50] Tom (PM): quality regression is a hard no for our top-tier customers. can you do canary rollouts between model variants?
[03:56] Priya (SE): yes our rollout system supports canary and A/B with automatic fallback to previous version on metric drift. we can tie evals to your prompt sets to monitor regressions.
[04:05] Maya (ML Eng): we run a lot of sampling for n-best lists; how does that impact token/sec and p95?

[04:10] Priya (SE): sampling increases per-call compute but often it's the same number of tokens; the difference in latency depends on decoding strategy. For high-throughput sampling we recommend batching and lower temperature parallelism where possible.
[04:20] Jordan (Infra): can you talk to the storage side — are logs persisted, where, and can we ship them to our SIEM?
[04:25] Alex (AE): audit logs can be shipped to your S3 or pushed to a SIEM via secure delivery. For Private deployments logs remain in your environment.
[04:31] Sana (Security): encryption at rest and in transit? Bring your own keys?
[04:34] Alex (AE): yes both in transit and at rest. BYOK is available for Dedicated and Private through KMS/HSM integrations.
[04:40] Evan (CTO): ok back to p95 numbers — if we need 200ms p95 for short flows, is that achievable on Hosted in eu without dedicated?

[04:47] Priya (SE): it's possible with smaller quantized models and regional endpoints, but depends on prompt length and request size. For 50-200 token prompts you can hit ~150-220ms p95 on Hosted eu, but the guarantee comes with Dedicated.
[04:59] Tom (PM): what's the expected per-token cost delta between hosted and dedicated for our volume?

[05:04] Alex (AE): rough rule: hosted is higher per-token due to multi-tenancy but no upfront. Dedicated amortizes GPU cost — at your projected sustained baseline we'd expect 30-45% lower unit cost on Dedicated assuming committed usage.
[05:15] Maya (ML Eng): are there tooling hooks for profiling latency per step? we want per-layer breakdown to see where the time goes.

[05:21] Priya (SE): yes Redwood Console exposes per-token latency, kernel-level breakdowns (attention vs matmul), and trace spans for model load, decode, network. We can share a sample trace dashboard.
[05:30] Jordan (Infra): can you run the scaling benchmark from our network? we'd prefer to avoid synthetic traffic that doesn't mirror our ingress path.
[05:35] Priya (SE): we can run tests using your network IPs via a temporary peering or use our synthetic clients that simulate your egress. For private we can run on-prem package directly.

[05:44] Alex (AE): i'll propose a benchmark plan: 1) Priya runs a hosted small-sample test in eu-west with your prompts to measure first-token and end-to-end; 2) scale test with 50/100/200 concurrent streams to measure token/sec and p95; 3) a Dedicated pilot if hosted doesn't meet p95. Sound ok?
[05:58] Evan (CTO): yes. For the scale test, please capture tail latencies at p50, p90, p95, p99, and token/sec throughput. Also include cold-start quantiles.
[06:09] Priya (SE): noted. we'll capture the quantiles and include CPU/GPU utilization and mem usage in the report.
[06:16] Tom (PM): timeline wise we want a go/no-go on hosting mode in 2 weeks. can you commit to the benchmarks in that window?
[06:22] Alex (AE): yes we'll aim to deliver initial benchmarks and pricing in ~72 hours for the hosted micro-tests and full scale in 7 days.
[06:29] Maya (ML Eng): one more question - how do you handle partial failure in streaming? if a worker drops mid-stream do you re-route?

[06:34] Priya (SE): we have session affinity and automatic fallback; if a worker fails we attempt to resume from the last KV checkpoint or fallback to a compatible model instance. There can be a brief retry window but we minimize user-facing interruptions.
[06:45] Jordan (Infra): what's the SLA for Dedicated? uptime/latency?
[06:48] Alex (AE): Dedicated SLAs include 99.9% uptime and latency targets we can negotiate per contract — we also offer priority routing during capacity constraints.
[06:56] Sana (Security): contractually we need data deletion guarantees and audit records retention periods, plus penetration test reports.
[07:02] Alex (AE): we'll include retention and deletion language and PoVs, and can share recent pentest summary and SOC2 report under NDA.

[07:08] Evan (CTO): ok call is getting long — good detail — let's do the bench plan and reconvene. we might also ask for a short POC where we route a small percent of traffic to Redwood to validate live behavior.
[07:17] Priya (SE): we can support a POC with traffic mirroring or shadow mode, and a small canary with actual users. For cost control we can cap concurrency and token limits for the POC.
[07:24] Tom (PM): what's the acceptance criteria for POC? we'll need p95 numbers and no quality regressions on our eval set.
[07:30] Alex (AE): acceptance: p95 at or below proposed targets, no regression on quality metrics for your prompts, network/security controls in place. We'll put that in the SOW.
[07:36] Maya (ML Eng): we will provide the eval prompt set and expected metrics.
[07:40] Jordan (Infra): and we'll provide source IPs and a sample ingress path for the benchmarking nodes.
[07:45] Priya (SE): great. i'll include instrumentation details: what metrics we emit, export formats (Prometheus, CSV) and what logs we can deliver for your SIEM.

[07:55] Alex (AE): action recap — i'll send SOC2/KMS/docs, pricing and the hosted vs dedicated TCO, priya will run the benchmarks, maya will send prompt set, jordan will share network profile. we'll target a technical deep-dive next week.
[08:07] Evan (CTO): thanks all. any final Qs?
[08:10] Sana (Security): just one: for BYOK can keys be rotated without service interruption?
[08:14] Priya (SE): yes we support key rotation workflows integrated with KMS and our runtime supports hot swap of encryption keys without downtime for dedicated/private modes.
[08:21] Tom (PM): perfect. that's it from me.
[08:23] Alex (AE): great — i'll follow up with the notes and links. thanks everyone — we'll send the benchmark plan by end of day.
[08:30] Evan (CTO): thanks alex, priya. bye.
